items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I joined the band. When I joined the band, we had to talk money. I’m talking money with George Hart, the road manager. ... Lionel, I guess he didn’t have anything to say about anything. He just played the vibes.

ctx.x: About how long did you study? Do you remember how many years?

Yes. Five years. From 9 to 14. That’s when I heard Lionel Hampton and heard Arnett Cobb play Flyin’ Home. The piano paled that afternoon. I’d never heard a big band play live. When that curtain opened – well, they started to play before the curtain

opened. So the anticipation was really high. When the curtain started to open slowly, I saw the bright lights shining on all these golden instruments. The drummer was playing, and the bass player’s – I’d never seen anything like that in my life. They were playing Flyin’ Home. Earl Bostic was the saxophone player in the band at that time, too. They played this thing, and they played the interlude. This fellow got up, stepped out in front of the band. I said, I wonder what the heck is he going to do? The microphone…
